title: Pairs with small singular locus
statement: A small-singular-locus pair consists of a scheme $X$ over $\mathbf Q$, reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, equivalently with a finite affine Noetherian cover), with every affine coordinate ring quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], and a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $I$ defining an effective Cartier divisor $D\subseteq X$, meaning $I$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-invertible-ideal]. Every $x\in X$ whose local ring is not regular belongs to $|D|$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Require that for some $n\geq0$, schemes $V_i$, fields $K_i$ of characteristic zero, and structure maps $s_i:V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the abstract scheme $D$ is isomorphic to $\coprod_{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}V_i$. The fields may differ. The existence of a presentation is a condition on the pair, not extra chosen data. The empty scheme and empty divisor are allowed, as are finite disjoint unions.

source.place: Temkin, arXiv:0904.1592v2, §3.4.2, Theorem 3.4.1 and Remark 3.4.2(i), printed pp.25–26; the reduced-input category of lem-per-small-singular-locus-resolution.
